page: Amazon Web Services d3en.6xlarge is a dense storage instance optimized for network and EBS throughput. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 24 vCPUs and 12 physical cores operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The system features 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. A key characteristic of this instance is its massive local storage capacity, offering 167,760 GB of local HDD storage. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as the stress-ng single-core score of 1327.3 and Geekbench single-core score of 1056.0, fall into the lower tier. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 20,993.88 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,267.0. Memory bandwidth is stable, reaching 1127.65 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 108.25 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Database operations perform reliably, with Redis SET operations achieving 20.06 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring 7,753.73.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the d3en.6xlarge offers high storage density per resource unit, making it a viable option for workloads requiring massive local capacity without the premium cost of SSD-based storage. The tradeoff is the reliance on HDD media, which limits random I/O performance compared to solid-state alternatives. This instance is best suited for data-intensive workloads such as large-scale data warehousing, distributed file systems, log processing, and big data analytics where sequential read and write throughput on massive datasets is prioritized over low-latency random access.

Powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor, it features 24 vCPUs, 12 physical cores, and 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory. The defining feature of this instance is its 167,760 GB of local HDD storage, supported by a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps. This hardware profile provides high storage density, making it a cost-effective choice for sequential data processing. The d3en.6xlarge is highly suited for distributed file systems, big data analytics, data warehousing, and large-scale log processing applications.
